decisions.quote: We replicated Son, Ellis, and Yoo (2013) and extended Ellis et al.'s (2014) taxonomy of harmful and inadequate supervision by providing and testing cross-national comparative descriptive data about clinical supervision practices in the Republic of Ireland versus the United States.

decisions.quote: With over 560 citations reported on Google Scholar by April 2018, a publication by Juslin and Gabrielsson (1996) presented evidence supporting performers’ abilities to communicate, with high accuracy, their intended emotional expressions in music to listeners. Though there have been related studies published on this topic, there has yet to be a direct replication of this paper. A replication is warranted given the paper’s influence in the field and the implications of its results. The present experiment joins the recent replication effort by producing a five-lab replication using the original methodology.
decisions.reason: The supplied primary source text (Akkermans et al., 10.1080/02699931.2018.1541312) contains only the title, author list, and abstract (lines 1-4), and no prior adjudication or prior state file exists. The abstract states that the five-lab study is a direct replication of 'a publication by Juslin and Gabrielsson (1996)', whereas the shipped row (input_row_index 887) has reversed author order: Gabrielsson & Juslin (1996), 'Emotional Expression in Music Performance: Between the Performer's Intention and the Listener's Experience', Psychology of Music, 24(1), 68-91 (doi:10.1177/0305735696241007, verified in bibliography_metadata.json). Because the primary text is abstract-only and contains no reference list, title, or DOI for 'Juslin and Gabrielsson (1996)', the precise unresolved question is whether the abstract's citation 'Juslin and Gabrielsson (1996)' is an author-order inversion referring to shipped input_row_index 887 (Gabrielsson & Juslin, 1996, 10.1177/0305735696241007) or a distinct 1996 publication by Juslin and Gabrielsson, which requires the full text or reference list.

Xu (1993) is never cited in the Abstract, Introduction, Rationale, Method, or Results; instead, 'Very recent research by Xu (1993)' is introduced post-hoc in the Discussion (lines 602-670) to explain why infants in the 'impossible identity-correct arithmetic' control condition did not look longer when Ernie turned into Elmo, before a retrospective summary remark (lines 663-670) notes that this effect was demonstrated just as in Xu's (1993) 10-month-old subjects. Moreover, the reference list (lines 751-752) establishes that Xu (1993) is an unpublished conference presentation ('Paper presented at the biennial meeting of the Society for Research in Child Development, New Orleans, LA'), not a previously published empirical finding under the codebook. Thus, shipped input_row_index 2196 (Wynn, 1992) already captures the sole published target replicated by this study, and target_index 1 is post-hoc interpretive context citing an unpublished meeting presentation.

decisions.quote:
Diagnostic accuracy of a universal screening multiple gating procedure: A replication study.
Stephen P. Kilgus, Nathaniel P. von der Embse, Crystal N. Taylor, Michael P. Van Wie, Wesley A. Sims

The purpose of this diagnostic accuracy study was to evaluate the sensitivity and specificity (among other indicators) of three universal screening approaches, including the Social, Academic, and Emotional Behavior Risk Screener (SAEBRS), a SAEBRS-based teacher nomination tool, and a multiple gating procedure (MGP).
